#### Learning Objectives

By the end of this part of the practical you should be able to:

- Explain what R is and why it is useful for biological data analysis.
- Use some features of the RStudio interface.
- Use the R console and R scripts to run R code.

#### Learning Objectives

By the end of this part of the practical you should be able to:

- Use Quarto documents to run R code.
- Create a simple reproducible analysis using Quarto.
- Understand the benefits of writing clear, well-formatted and documented R code.

#### Learning Objectives

By the end of this part of the practical you should be able to:

- Explain what a function is and use some simple functions.
- Explain how and why we provide arguments to functions.
- Explain the concept of a variable and use variables in your code.
- Recognise and use common types of variable, including numeric, character and logical variables.

#### Learning Objectives

By the end of this part of the practical you should be able to:

- Install and load a package in R.
- Create and use vectors in R.
- Access individual elements of a vector using an index.
- Create and view a simple data frame.
- Recognise and read data stored in CSV format.
- Create a simple line plot in R using ggplot2.
